- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or flat (especially <0.3) — model fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 75+), producing exaggerated highs that fail to correct quickly.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak — model holds high prices too long after peaks, ignoring momentum reversal signals.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model often lags behind true price drops — especially in early 30d horizon.
- For 30d forecasts, model tends to overfit recent volatility — ignores longer-term trend persistence or mean reversion anchors.
- If sentiment is negative and price is above 73, model often fails to adjust downward — underestimates downside risk.
- Model exhibits “late correction” bias — true price drops occur after forecast peaks, especially when sentiment is weak or flat.
